feature_name: Cockpit as Autonomous Claude Code Session (Tauri)
description: The cockpit becomes a LIVING Claude Code session — not a Rust/React dashboard, but an actual Claude Code instance that thinks, decides, observes dev slots, detects PRDs, spawns support agents, and plans tasks. The Tauri backend spawns and manages the cockpit session, parses stream-json, and routes events to the React frontend.
goals: Cockpit IS a Claude Code session (--agent cockpit-brain, background, memory: project)
Rust backend manages cockpit process lifecycle (spawn, parse, terminate)
React frontend renders cockpit consciousness (Brain tab = live stream)
Cockpit observes dev slots via filesystem polling (worktrees, prd.json, status.json)
Cockpit spawns support agents via Claude Code subagent system
When idle, cockpit produces transverse deliverables autonomously
All events route through event_bus to React UI
non_goals: Cockpit does NOT replace the chat panel (left) — chat is user conversation
Cockpit does NOT launch dev slots from PRDs — that's chat+dispatch
No Agent SDK rewrite for v1 — use CLI headless mode

rust_backend: cockpit_session.rs — new service managing the cockpit Claude Code process
Parses stream-json line by line using stream_parser.rs (from PRD-43)
Routes events to event_bus: cockpit-thinking, cockpit-action, cockpit-decision, cockpit-loop
Stores cockpit session_id in DB for resume
Manages lifecycle: start on project load, stop on quit, resume on restart
react_frontend: CockpitBrainTab.tsx — becomes a live stream of cockpit consciousness
Subscribes to Tauri events: cockpit-thinking, cockpit-action, cockpit-decision
Renders: reasoning as dimmed text, tool calls as badges, decisions as highlights
Loop iterations as periodic pulse indicators
Replaces static COP display with live consciousness
agent_definition: tools: Read, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, Write, WebSearch, Agent(meta-monitor, transverse-producer)
permissionMode: auto, memory: project, background: true
Prompt: full mission brief with monitoring instructions

user_stories.title: cockpit-brain.md agent definition generator
user_stories.description: In cockpit_brain.rs, add function generate_cockpit_agent_definition(project_path, cop) -> Result<()>. Writes .claude/agents/cockpit-brain.md with: frontmatter (name, description, tools including Agent() for spawning sub-agents, model: inherit, permissionMode: auto, memory: project, background: true), body (full mission brief: what to observe, when to spawn agents, what deliverables to produce, how to use /loop, reaction rules for errors/budget/conflicts). Also generates support agent definitions: .claude/agents/meta-monitor.md (read-only, watches worktrees), .claude/agents/transverse-producer.md (writes .md deliverables), .claude/agents/specialist-{domain}.md (deep analysis). Expose as Tauri command: generate_cockpit_agent_definition.
tests: Agent() tool included for sub-agent spawning

user_stories.title: Cockpit session manager (Rust service)
user_stories.description: New file: src-tauri/src/services/cockpit_session.rs. CockpitSessionManager struct with: start_session(project_path) — spawns claude headless with cockpit-brain agent. Builds initial context prompt: project path, type, domain, active dev slots (from slot_repo), active PRD (scan for prd.json), recent git activity, previous cockpit memories. Launches via std::process::Command with stdout piped. Spawns tokio task to read stream-json line by line and emit events. stop_session() — sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL. resume_session(session_id) — uses --resume flag. is_alive() — checks process status. Global singleton accessible from commands. New Tauri commands: start_cockpit_session, stop_cockpit_session, get_cockpit_status. Register in main.rs. Session auto-starts when project is loaded (wire into app setup).
tests: cockpit session launches on project load

user_stories.title: Stream-json event router for cockpit
user_stories.description: Extend stream_parser.rs (or create cockpit_stream_parser.rs) to handle cockpit-specific events. Parse stream-json and categorize into cockpit event types: CockpitThinking (assistant text = reasoning), CockpitAction (tool_use = action being taken), CockpitDecision (text containing decision keywords: 'spawning', 'launching', 'detected', 'switching'), CockpitLoop (text from /loop iterations), CockpitSubagent (Agent tool calls). Emit via event_bus with new event names: 'cockpit-thinking', 'cockpit-action', 'cockpit-decision', 'cockpit-loop', 'cockpit-subagent'. Each event payload: timestamp, event_type, content (text or structured). Also continue routing to 'log-entry' for MCP LOGS panel.
tests: thinking events emitted for assistant text
events route to both cockpit and MCP logs

user_stories.title: Dev slot observation prompt
user_stories.description: The cockpit brain's initial prompt and /loop instructions tell it HOW to observe dev slots. The prompt includes: 'You have {N} dev agents running in parallel worktrees: Slot 1 (claude) at {path} on branch {branch} doing {task}. Monitor them by: 1) Run `git -C {worktree} diff --stat` to see what changed. 2) Check prd.json story statuses. 3) Look for test failures in logs. 4) Use /loop 30s to poll every 30 seconds. Report findings. When all stories are done, evaluate merge readiness.' This is part of the agent definition body, NOT hardcoded Rust logic. The cockpit brain uses Claude's own reasoning to decide what to do with the observations.
tests: prompt includes active dev slot info
git diff command suggested for monitoring

user_stories.title: PRD detection by cockpit brain
user_stories.description: The cockpit brain prompt instructs it to scan for PRD files: 'Periodically check for prd.json and prd-*.json in the project root. When you find one: 1) Read it to understand the feature being built. 2) Map stories to active dev slots. 3) Track completion progress. 4) Adjust your support agent strategy based on the PRD domain. When a new PRD appears, analyze it and plan transverse deliverables specific to this feature.' The cockpit uses Read tool + Glob tool to find PRDs. When it detects one, it logs: 'PRD detected: {feature_name} with {N} stories — planning support.' This replaces our custom PRD detection with Claude's own intelligence.
tests: transverse plan adjusts to PRD domain

user_stories.title: Support agent spawning via Agent() tool
user_stories.description: The cockpit brain can spawn support agents using the Agent() tool available in Claude Code. The cockpit prompt includes: 'You have access to these support agents via the Agent tool: @meta-monitor (watches dev worktrees, runs tests, reports quality), @transverse-producer (creates marketing, docs, strategy deliverables in .crossroads/deliverables/), @specialist-security, @specialist-pricing (domain experts). Spawn them when appropriate: meta-monitor when dev slots start, transverse-producer at 50% progress or when idle, specialists when domain patterns detected.' The cockpit decides autonomously when and which agents to spawn. Stream-json output will contain Agent tool_use events which we parse and display in the Brain tab as 'Spawning: @meta-monitor'.
tests: Agent tool calls visible in Brain tab

user_stories.title: Idle mode — autonomous initiative
user_stories.description: The cockpit prompt includes idle mode instructions: 'When no dev agents are running (all slots empty or completed): switch to initiative mode. In this mode: 1) Scan the project for improvements (missing tests, outdated deps, code quality issues). 2) Produce transverse deliverables if not done (README, API docs, deployment guide). 3) Run a lightweight security scan. 4) Generate a project health report in .crossroads/deliverables/health-report.md. 5) Prepare recommendations for the next session. Use /loop 5m in idle mode (slower polling). Stop initiative mode when new dev slots launch.' The cockpit's initiative is driven by Claude's reasoning, not hardcoded triggers.
tests: idle mode activates when no dev slots

user_stories.title: Brain tab — live consciousness stream (React)
user_stories.description: Rewrite CockpitBrainTab.tsx to render the cockpit's live stream instead of static COP data. Subscribe to Tauri events: 'cockpit-thinking' → dimmed italic text (inner monologue), 'cockpit-action' → colored badges [Read] [Bash] [Agent] with target, 'cockpit-decision' → highlighted entry with green left border, 'cockpit-loop' → subtle pulse dot with timestamp, 'cockpit-subagent' → agent name badge with status. Layout: scrolling feed of entries (newest at bottom), auto-scroll, max 200 entries with FIFO. Header shows: cockpit status (alive/idle/error), uptime, memory usage. Empty state: 'Cockpit brain starting...' with pulse animation. This makes the cockpit feel ALIVE — you can see it thinking, deciding, and acting in real-time.
tests: tool calls show as colored badges
